memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Appointment booked for 2025-04-15 at 10:00 with Dr Nandini Kulkarni (D06) for dyslipidaemia review.

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
function: reports mild fatigue after work, able to perform lab duties without difficulty.
cognition: Mini-Cog score 4/5 (recall 3, clock draw normal), negative screen.
falls: no falls in past 12 months; gait steady; timed up-and-go 9 seconds, normal.
medicines: 0 regular; starting lipid-lowering therapy today.
mood: denies depression or anxiety; PHQ-2 not done.
carers: lives alone; no formal carer.
goals: "I want to keep my cholesterol under control and stay active at work."

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
atorvastatin 10 mg HS
rosuvastatin 10 mg OD
fenofibrate 145 mg OD

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Fasting lipid profile: LDL 115 mg/dL (<100 optimal), HDL 44 mg/dL (>40), triglycerides 162 mg/dL (<150 borderline). LFT: ALT 30 U/L (≤40), AST 26 U/L (≤40), bilirubin 0.9 mg/dL (≤1.2). CK 210 U/L (≤200 slight rise).

memories.author: D06
memories.text: Resting ECG: sinus rhythm 78 bpm, no ST‑T changes, no left ventricular hypertrophy. Normal study.

memories.author: D06
memories.text: Referral to Dr S. Patel, Cardiology, for evaluation of persistent borderline triglycerides and CK elevation. Request lipid‑guided therapy advice and cardiac risk assessment.

memories.author: D06
memories.text: Cardiology reply: triglycerides likely diet‑related; CK rise mild, possibly statin‑related. Recommend continue current statin, monitor CK, consider fenofibrate pause if CK >3×ULN. No cardiac pathology.
